milestones.title: Government starts making electricity
milestones.text: The South Coast Irrigation Service's Carite plant becomes the first hydro plant owned by the government of Puerto Rico.

milestones.title: Water Resources Authority created
milestones.text: The Autoridad de las Fuentes Fluviales, PREPA's predecessor, is created as a public corporation able to issue its own bonds.

milestones.title: Revenue bond trust agreement
milestones.text: PREPA signs the trust agreement under which it issues power revenue bonds, payable only from its own revenues. It still governs PREPA's bonds.

milestones.title: Renamed PREPA
milestones.text: Act 57-1979 renames the authority the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority, reflecting the shift from hydro to oil. By then nearly all generation burned oil.

milestones.title: Hurricane María and bankruptcy
milestones.text: PREPA, carrying about $9 billion of debt, enters Title III bankruptcy under PROMESA on July 2, 2017. Hurricane María devastates the grid that September.

milestones.title: LUMA takes over the grid
milestones.text: On June 1, 2021, LUMA Energy begins operating transmission and distribution under a 15-year contract.

milestones.title: Genera PR takes over the plants
milestones.text: On July 1, 2023, Genera PR, a New Fortress Energy subsidiary, begins operating PREPA's non-hydro power plants. PREPA keeps running the hydro plants; the plants remain public property.
